# Set up R environment
```{r setup}
# load libraries
library(lavaan)
library(power4mome)
library(broom)
library(rempsyc)
library(tidyverse)
library(flextable)

# define seed for reproducibility
seed <- 23571113

```

# Define model structures
```{r models}
# define model structure for moderation models
mod_model <-
  "
  y ~ x1 + w + x1:w + control
  "

# define model structure for theoretical model one
model_one <- 
    "
  # Regressions
    fm1 ~ fx
    m2 ~ fx
    y ~ fx + fm1 + m2
  # Variances
    fm1 ~~ m2
    "

# define model structure for theoretical model one
model_two <-
    "
  # Regressions
    fm1 ~ fx
    m2 ~ fx
    m3 ~ fx + fm1 + m2
    fm4 ~ fm1
    m5 ~ m2
    y ~ m3 + fm4 + m5
  # Variances
    fm1 ~~ m2
    fm4 ~~ m5
    "
```

# Estimate effect sizes and reliability for latent variables
```{r estimates}
# estimate effect sizes for moderation models
mod_model_es <-
  "
  .beta.: l
  y ~ x1: m
  y ~ w: l
  y ~ x1:w: .15
  "

# estimate effect sizes for theoretical model one
model_one_es <-
  "
  fm1 ~ fx: m
  m2 ~ fx: m
  y ~ fx: m
  y ~ fm1: m
  y ~ m2: m
  fm1 ~~ m2: m
  "

# estimate effect sizes for theoretical model two
model_two_es <-
  "
  fm1 ~ fx: m
  m2 ~ fx: m
  m3 ~ fx: m
  m3 ~ fm1: m
  m3 ~ m2: m
  fm4 ~ fm1: l
  m5 ~ m2: l
  y ~ m3: l
  y ~ fm4: m
  y ~ m5: m
  fm1 ~~ m2: m
  fm4 ~~ m5: m
  "

# define how many indicators each latent variable has for model one
k1 <- c(fx = 3,
       fm1 = 4)

# define expected reliability for model one latent variables
model_rel1 <- c(fx = .85,
               fm1 = .9)

# define how many indicators each latent variable has for model two

k2 <- c(fx = 4,
        fm1 = 4,
        fm4 = 4)

# define expectedd reliabilities for model two latent variables
model_rel2 <- c(fx = .85,
        fm1 = .9,
        fm4 = .9)


```
# Check model structure
```{r model_check}

# Moderation model check
mod_model_check <-power4test(nrep=2,
                            model= mod_model,
                            pop_es = mod_model_es,
                            n = 50,
                            iseed = seed)
mod_model_check

# Theoretical model 1 check
model_one_check <-power4test(nrep=2,
                            model= model_one,
                            pop_es = model_one_es,
                            number_of_indicators = k1,
                            reliability = model_rel1,
                            n = 50,
                            iseed = seed)
model_one_check

# Theoretical model 2 check
model_two_check <- power4test(nrep = 2,
                  model = model_two,
                  pop_es = model_two_es,
                  number_of_indicators = k2,
                  reliability = model_rel2,
                  n = 50,
                  iseed = seed)

model_two_check

```
# Power Analysis for moderation models
```{r mod_model}
# free up locked memory prior to computation
gc()

# calculate initial simulation for moderation model fit
mod_model_out <-power4test(nrep=200,
                            model= mod_model,
                            pop_es = mod_model_es,
                            n = 100,
                            R = 2000,
                            ci_type = "mc",
                            fit_model_args = list(fit_function = "lm"),
                            test_fun = test_moderation,
                            iseed = seed,
                            parallel = TRUE)
mod_model_out



# recalculate estimate power and effect sizes across the range of possible Ns
mod_model_out_n <- power4test_by_n(mod_model_out, n = c(300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350))

# calculate rejection rates for the interaction effect across all sample sizes
mod_model_rates <- rejection_rates(mod_model_out_n)

# plot power by sample size
mod_model_rates %>%
  ggplot(aes(n, reject)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .80, linetype = "dashed", color = c("red")) +
    annotate("text", x = 301, y = .81, label = "B = .80", color = "red") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(300, 350), ylim = c(0.5, 0.99)) +
    theme_classic()


# isolate relevant columns and arrange by sample size
mod_model_rates_out <- mod_model_rates %>%
  select(n, test, est, reject, reject_ci_lo, reject_ci_hi) %>%
  arrange(n)


# rename collumns to be more legibly
colnames(mod_model_rates_out) <- c("n","effect","r", "B", "Lower CI", "Upper CI")

# replace test labels with more meaninful labels
tests <- rep(c("x:w->y"), 6)
mod_model_rates_out$effect <- tests

# convert dataframe to a nice looking table
mod_model_stats_table <- nice_table(mod_model_rates_out,
                          title = c("Table 1", "Estimated power for moderation models"),
                          note = "Estimates generated using Monte-Carlo simulation with 2000 replications. Estimated r indicates mean effect size across repolications.")

# save table to MS word for easy insertion in manuscript
flextable::save_as_docx(mod_model_stats_table, path = "./output/nice_table1.docx")

```
# Power analysis for theoretical model one
```{r analyze_model_one}
# free up locked memory prior to computation
gc()

# simulate initial model with the first in direct path via fm1
lm1_fit1 <- power4test(nrep=200,
                            model= model_one,
                            pop_es = model_one_es,
                            number_of_indicators = k1,
                            reliability = model_rel1,
                            n = 200,
                            R = 2000,
                            ci_type = "mc",
                            test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
                            test_args = list(
                              x = "fx",
                              m = "fm1",
                              y = "fy",
                              mc_ci = TRUE
                            ),
                            iseed = seed,
                            parallel = TRUE)
lm1_fit1

# add second parralel path through m2 to model and re-simulate fit
lm1_out <- power4test(
  object = lm1_fit1,
  test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
  test_args = list(x = "fx", m = "m2", y = "fy", mc_ci = TRUE),
  test_name = "fx_m2_fy"
)

# simulate model across possible sample sizes
lm1_out_n <- power4test_by_n(lm1_out, n = c(300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350))

# calculate rejection rates for each path and sample size
lm1_rates <- rejection_rates(lm1_out_n)

# replace test column with more meaningful path labels
tests <- rep(c("fx->fm1->fy", "fx->m2->fy"), 6)
lm1_rates$test <- tests

# plot estimate power by sample size and pathway
lm1_rates %>%
  ggplot(aes(n, reject, colour = test)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .80, linetype = "dashed", color = c("red")) +
    annotate("text", x = 301, y = .81, label = "B = .80", color = "red") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(300, 350), ylim = c(0.5, 0.99)) +
    theme_classic()


# select important sample sizes, extract important columns, and arrange by sample size
lm1_rates_out <- lm1_rates %>%
  filter(n %in% c(300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350)) %>%
  select(n, test, est, reject, reject_ci_lo, reject_ci_hi) %>%
  arrange(n)

# rename columns to be more useful
colnames(lm1_rates_out) <- c("n", "Path", "r", "B", "Lower CI", "Upper CI")

# convert table to a nice looking data frame
lm1_stats_table <- nice_table(lm1_rates_out,
                          title = c("Table 2", "Estimated power for theoretical model 1 by pathway"),
                          note = "Estimates generated using Monte-Carlo simulation with 2000 replications. Estimated r indicates mean effect size across repolications.")

# save nice table to MS word doc for easy insertion in manuscript
flextable::save_as_docx(lm1_stats_table, path = "./output/nice_table2.docx")

```
# Power analysis for theoretical model 2
```{r analyze_model_2}
# free up locked memory prior to computation
gc()

# Simulate initial model fit considering only the simple moderation path by m3
lm2_single_fit <-power4test(nrep=200,
                            model= model_two,
                            pop_es = model_two_es,
                            number_of_indicators = k2,
                            reliability = model_rel2,
                            n = 200,
                            R = 2000,
                            ci_type = "mc",
                            test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
                            test_args = list(
                              x = "fx",
                              m = "m3",
                              y = "y",
                              mc_ci = TRUE
                            ),
                            iseed = seed,
                            parallel = TRUE)

# Re-simulate after adding first serial path via fm1 and m3
lm2_serial1 <- power4test(
  object = lm2_single_fit,
  test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
  test_args = list(x = "fx", m = c("fm1", "m3"), y = "y", mc_ci = TRUE),
  test_name = "fx_fm1_m3_y"
)

# Re-simulate after adding second serial path via m2 and m3
lm2_serial2 <- power4test(
  object = lm2_serial1,
  test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
  test_args = list(x = "fx", m = c("m2", "m3"), y = "y", mc_ci = TRUE),
  test_name = "fx_m2_m3_y"
)

# Re-simulate after adding first parallel path via fm1 and fm4
lm2_sp1 <- power4test(
  object = lm2_serial2,
  test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
  test_args = list(x = "fx", m = c("fm1", "fm4"), y = "y", mc_ci = TRUE),
  test_name = "fx_fm1_fm4_y"
)

# Re-simulate after adding second parallel path via m2 and m5
lm2_full <- power4test(
  object = lm2_sp1,
  test_fun = test_indirect_effect,
  test_args = list(x = "fx", m = c("m2", "m5"), y = "y", mc_ci = TRUE),
  test_name = "fx_m2_m5_y"
)

lm2_full

# simualte data across the range of sample sizes
lm2_out_n <- power4test_by_n(lm2_full, n = c(150, 155, 160, 165, 170, 175))

# calculate rejection rates across possible sample sizes for each indirect path
lm2_rates <- rejection_rates(lm2_out_n)




 # replace tests column with more meaningful path labels
tests <- rep(c("fx->m3->y", "fx->fm1->m3->y", "fx->m2->m3->y","fx->fm1->fm4->y","fx->m2->m5->y"), 6)
lm2_rates$test <- tests

# plot rejection rates for model two by sample size and pathway
lm2_rates %>%
  ggplot(aes(n, reject, colour = test)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .80, linetype = "dashed", color = c("red")) +
  annotate("text", x = 151, y = .81, label = "B = .80", color = "red") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(150, 175), ylim = c(0.5, 0.99)) +
  theme_classic()

# pull important sample sizes, isolate important collumns, and arrange by sample size
lm2_rates_out <- lm2_rates %>%
  filter(n %in% c(150, 165, 175, 200)) %>%
  select(n, test, est, reject, reject_ci_lo, reject_ci_hi) %>%
  arrange(n)

# update column names to make table more legible
colnames(lm2_rates_out) <- c("n", "Path", "r", "B", "Lower CI", "Upper CI")

# convert dataframe to a nice looking table
lm2_stats_table <- nice_table(lm2_rates_out,
                          title = c("Table 3", "Estimated power for theoretical model 3 by pathway"),
                          note = "Estimates generated using Monte-Carlo simulation with 2000 replications. Estimated r indicates mean effect size across repolications.")

# save table to MS word doc for easy insertion into manuscript
flextable::save_as_docx(lm2_stats_table, path = "./output/nice_table3.docx")
```
